exercise.name: Decline Oblique Crunch
steps: Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back.
Curl up and twist so one shoulder moves toward the opposite knee.
Lower slowly and switch sides each rep.
exercise.one_line_summary: Feet hooked on a 20 deg decline bench, arms crossed. Start lying back; end curled half way up with the trunk twisted so the right shoulder comes across toward the left knee. Obliques are the target, abs help.

setup.target: Pad tilted 20 deg, high end 0.80 m, the head end lower than the feet.
setup.why: Library step 1: feet hooked under the pads of a decline bench; the slope makes the trunk lift against more of gravity than on the floor.

setup.target: Knees bent over the knee roll, ankles under the front roller.
setup.tolerance: feet stay under the roller in both pictures
setup.why: Library step 1. Hooked feet let the hip flexors pull, which S1 shows as high rectus femoris in the bent-knee sit-up.

setup.target: Arms crossed on the chest, fists on the chest.
setup.tolerance: forearms on the chest, not pulling the head
setup.why: Library step 2 (sit-up); crossed arms keep the hands off the neck.

muscles.emg: Obliques greatest in the crunch and bent-knee sit-up (S1); twisting adds the rotation they produce.
muscles.role: Main mover: turns and curls the rib cage toward the opposite hip.
muscles.surface: Sides of the waist from the lower ribs to the hip bone.
The two vertical bands down the front of the belly, lower ribs to the pubic bone.

muscles.role: Holds the hooked legs; not lit.
muscles.surface: Front of the hip and the top of the thigh.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbow swings across while the shoulders stay square.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The obliques do little; the shoulder must cross.

sources.citation: Escamilla RF, McTaggart MS, Fricklas EJ, et al. 2006. An electromyographic analysis of commercial and common abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 36(2):45-57. doi:10.2519/jospt.2006.36.2.45
sources.what_it_gave: Upper/lower rectus abdominis greatest in the crunch (with Ab Slide, Torso Track); obliques greatest in the crunch and bent-knee sit-up; rectus femoris greatest in the bent-knee sit-up.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
sources.what_it_gave: Erector spinae highest in back extensions (~63% MVIC on the floor, ~56% on a bench); V-sits ~80% MVIC rectus abdominis; adding a stability ball raises core EMG; sit-ups and curl-ups the classic core exercises.
The steps the app shows; the pictures must match them.

clip_check.check: End: right shoulder clearly across toward the left knee
